See exact pricing, free 750 credits, and real cost examples.", "targetKeyword": "ai website builder with transparent pricing", "category": "Feature", "bodyHtml": "

Why \"transparent pricing\" is the real question to ask an AI website builder

Ask around and you'll hear the same complaint about AI website builders: the sticker price is not the real price. A tool advertises an \"unlimited\" plan, then quietly throttles you once you're a heavy user. Or it sells \"credits,\" but burns them the moment you hit Generate, even if the build fails to compile and you get nothing usable back. Bill shock is common enough in this category that it has become an expected cost of doing business, and most builders never explain what a credit actually buys.

Kodely was built around a different idea: the price should reflect what a generation actually costs to run, not an arbitrary markup, and you should never pay for output you didn't get. That single rule shapes everything below, from the credit system to the failed-build policy to the pricing table itself.

How Kodely's credit system works

When you describe a site in Kodely's chat interface, it generates a real application: a Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 project made of actual component files, not a flat HTML mockup. You watch a live preview render the compiled app as it's built. Every generation, whether it's the first build or a small follow-up change, costs a number of credits tied to the real cost of producing it.

You start with 750 credits free on signup, no credit card required, which is enough to build and iterate on a first project before you have to decide whether to pay anything at all. From there, credits are simple to buy and they never expire. A $9 top-up doesn't quietly vanish after 30 days if you don't get around to using it.

You're never charged for a build that fails

This is the part most credit-based tools skip: if a generation fails to compile, Kodely does not charge you for it. The system automatically runs one repair attempt first. If that repair succeeds, you get a working build. If it still fails, your credits are untouched, because you're only charged for output that actually works. That's a deliberate transparency feature, not a fallback bug fix, and it's the practical difference between credits as a real cost meter and credits as a subscription in disguise.

Real cost examples

Numbers make this concrete:

  • A typical first build, the initial site generated from your description, runs roughly 100 to 150 credits.
  • A follow-up change, like adjusting a section or adding a new page, usually costs a similar amount, in that same rough range per meaningful edit.

That means the free 750-credit signup allowance covers a first build plus several rounds of edits before you need to top up, and every paid tier below is sized around multiples of that same real usage.

Full pricing table

PlanPriceCreditsNotes
Free$0750 creditsOn signup, no credit card required
Starter top-up$9500 creditsCredits never expire
Most popular$402,500 creditsCredits never expire
Power top-up$906,000 creditsCredits never expire

There's no hidden \"Agency\" tier and no fine print underneath this table. The credit system above is the entire pricing model. See the full breakdown on the pricing page.

FAQ

Do credits expire?

No. Once purchased, credits stay on your account until you use them.

What do I actually get for free?

750 credits on signup, no credit card required, enough for a first build and several edits before you need to decide whether to pay anything.

What kind of site does Kodely actually build?

A real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application made of genuine component files, with a live preview of the compiled app as it's generated. One click publishes it to a free public subdomain like yourproject.kodely.site.

Can I keep editing after I publish?

Yes. Describe the change in chat and Kodely edits the real components behind your site. Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so rolling back to an earlier version is free.

Can I download or export the code?

Not yet. You can view and copy the generated source files directly in the app's code view, but there's no zip export or download option today.

Does Kodely support custom domains or a backend?

Not yet. Publishing today gives you a subdomain at yourproject.kodely.site, and generation is frontend-only, so there's no database, authentication, or payments generation.

Is a published site checked for anything before it goes live?

Yes. Every publish is scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live.

If you'd rather see how the numbers work on your own project than take them on faith, the fastest way is to try it. Start building free and watch exactly what each generation costs.
